method: OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-transcribe applied once to each of five fixed portions of the official publisher episode. Controller compared complete returned text with canonical YouTube captions and identified the same sustained utterances, turns and breaks.

alignment.basis: Matching complete utterances; exact podcast and YouTube timestamps differ because of insertions. No constant offset assumed.

parts.canonicalCoverageApprox: 1:17:40 through final statements and publisher-only outro

findings.finding: Copan’s enemy-loving Jesus concession, Christocentric/cruciform reading, actual/textual distinction, canonical continuity and unresolved-tension qualifications are confirmed. He primarily targets Boyd’s approach; do not transfer every criticism to Rauser.

Rauser’s Longman/Webb illustrations, express qualification of Copan’s sophistication, fallible God-given moral intuition, plenary inspiration, divine authorial inerrancy and 2 Timothy 3:14–17 reference are confirmed. Divine intent can diverge from human intent; this is not rejection of Christianity.

Marcionite label discussion and mutual caution confirmed. Rauser describes classical theism as atemporal, impassible and immutable, not a temporal God. Copan’s appeal to Matthew 5 and Matthew 23 and accommodation response are confirmed. A possible Moses/Jesus verbal or recognition substitution in the repudiation sentence is not eligible as an independent claim, quote or coherence penalty.

Rauser distinguishes the theological centrality of resurrection from Jericho’s historicity, explicitly qualifies his own Mark date, and contrasts the wide Joshua dating range. Scholar-name spelling remains uncertain and must not justify a rating. The inference about historical confidence is assessable as his argument, not an externally established consensus.

Copan affirms historical core plus strong hyperbole, merisms, sports and ancient royal boasts, Numbers 21 versus Deuteronomy 2–3, Sihon/Og and 1 Samuel 15/14:48 with Kenite departure and surviving Amalekites. Names and references are recognizable across the independent audio transcript; exact spellings in canonical quotations remain unchanged.

Rauser explicitly grants hyperbole but cites Rahab’s family, Joshua 6:21/23, return to Ai at Joshua 8:24 and Kitchen’s less-mobile inhabitants. Copan appeals to Richard Hess, citadels, military commanders, exceptional Rahab and absent pottery. His pottery phrasing remains imprecise in both automatic renderings: assess the asserted citadel inference, never a fabricated precise pottery taxonomy or caption disfluency penalty.

Drive-out priority, Joshua obedience with survivors, New Testament continuity and Jude 5 Jesus reading are confirmed. Copan mentions 1 Corinthians 10, Revelation 2, Ananias/Sapphira, corrects Acts 13 to Acts 12, and corrects Acts to Romans 11:22. The phrase attributing historical necessity to Rauser is unclear in both renderings; do not infer a concession or contradiction from that clause.

Rauser’s Joshua 8:25 civilian challenge, distinction between Copan and sweeping genocide defenders, concession of hyperbole, ethnic-cleansing definition and spoken 1948 genocide convention wording are confirmed. Residential-school comparison is his analogy. Verification authenticates what he argues, not the legal correctness of his application.

Short correction is Copan; the page-212 quotation and German-language counterexample are Rauser; the response beginning couldn’t you say Nazism was the religion is Copan. Ownership must not combine these into a single Copan source span. Asherah poles, Shechem, Rahab, covenant inclusion and continued Canaanite presence are confirmed as Copan’s examples.

Copan describes herem/haram range including killing, exile and setting apart for sacred use, with Deuteronomy 8, Jeremiah 25 and Leviticus 27 examples and Walton identity interpretation. This confirms the distinction being asserted without independently validating the Hebrew or exegesis.

Copan’s renewed citadel/flight claim and cross-Testament judgment examples confirmed. Avoid deriving a penalty from unclear citation assignment around 1 Corinthians 10/Jude 5; the independently clear Jesus-judgment argument is eligible.

Rauser’s moral-intuition test and spiritualizing alternatives confirmed: Origen/Gregory of Nyssa, exilic audience, Rahab/Achan boundary challenge and moral-errantist option. He does not settle on one option. Contemporary interpreter spelling remains uncertain. Copan responds with New Testament severity, conflicting intuitions and Abraham’s expectation of Isaac’s return; assess claimed contextual relevance, not uncertain name spelling.

Both actual closings are complete. Rauser cites Middleton, intrinsic wrongness, and future repetition concern tied to another scholar’s Revelation 19 interpretation; do not impute that scholar’s openness to Copan. Copan explicitly calls conquest unique and unrepeatable, rejects some divine commands, cites Jeremiah on infant sacrifice, and offers the hijacked-airplane contextual exception. All qualifications remain required.

residualLimitations: Both sources are automatic transcriptions; their agreement does not establish exact literal wording where either remains corrupt.
Uncertain proper-name spelling, isolated biblical numbering slips, ambiguous negations and quoted taxonomy cannot produce score penalties.
No source-excluded argument is reintroduced by audio verification.
Canonical exact quotations may not be silently rewritten using secondary text.
